title: Wind Chime
mood: a grief you have no standing to feel
subject: the neighbour's wind chime you resented for fourteen years and now miss
caption: American slowcore built around pedal steel. Pedal steel playing long weeping swells with audible bar movement, baritone electric guitar striking single clean notes and letting them ring out fully, brushed snare keeping a bare pulse, upright bass played soft and slow, one tremolo guitar note under the final chorus. Extremely sparse and slow with long decays and deliberate silence between phrases, nothing filling the gaps. Low male voice, almost spoken, recorded very close with breath left in, no vibrato and no belting. 62 BPM, C major. A grief you have no standing to feel. No drum kit fills, no synth, no strings section, no chorus lift, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - pedal steel and brushed snare]

[Verse 1]
Fourteen years that thing hung on her porch
Cheap aluminum, four tubes, one of them too short
I counted every night I couldn't sleep through it
I had a whole speech ready. Never gave it.

[Chorus]
Now the hook is still there and nothing's on it
And I stand at my window like an idiot, waiting
I didn't know I had memorized it
I didn't know it was the sound of somebody being home

[Verse 2]
Her son came with a truck on a Tuesday
Took the chairs, the pots, the chime. The hook stayed.
He waved at me. I waved back. That's the most we ever did.
Fourteen years of a sound and I never learned her last name

[Chorus]
Now the hook is still there and nothing's on it
And I stand at my window like an idiot, listening
I didn't know I had memorized it
I didn't know it was the sound of somebody being home

[Bridge - pedal steel alone]
I bought one. Hung it on my own porch.
Wrong pitch. Course it is.

[Outro - pedal steel, fading]
Four tubes, one of them too short
I'll leave it up
